Retrieved via Exa web_fetch. NPR, "U.S. strikes bridges in Iran; Tehran targets U.S. bases in the Gulf." Posted 7:13 AM ET July 17 2026.

- US and Iran expanded targets in latest round of strikes Friday, as fighting over control of the Strait of Hormuz reignites fears of all-out war.
- US struck Iranian air defence sites and military logistics infrastructure. Iran said targets included SIX BRIDGES in Hormozgan province facing the waterway, plus power infrastructure.
- Legal scholars warned attacks on infrastructure with wide civilian use could in some circumstances constitute a war crime under international law.
- President Trump threatened to strike Iranian bridges this week if Iran failed to return to talks to end the war.
- Iranian state media: at least SEVEN people killed and 20 wounded in the latest US strikes on infrastructure. Iranian health officials: 38 people killed and over 400 wounded in the past week.
- Overnight US strikes appeared to destroy a maritime control tower at Iranian port of Chabahar (Gulf of Oman). US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth shared a photo of the collapsing tower on social media.
- Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman; also claimed attack on US special forces at al-Tanf in Syria (former US outpost, US withdrew Feb).
- Authorities in Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar (key mediator) said their air defences were intercepting hostile attacks Friday. Jordan also staved off Iranian missiles per state media.
- Iranian strikes reported in Iraq's Kurdistan region, where at least EIGHT opposition fighters were killed, per the Kurdish Iranian opposition group.
- US reinstated a military blockade on ships entering/exiting Iranian ports earlier this week; says strikes aimed at "degrading Iranian military capabilities and holding Iran accountable for recent attacks on commercial shipping."
- Since reimposing blockade, US said it "redirected" three vessels, struck and disabled an oil tanker that disobeyed orders, and boarded one to ensure compliance. Oil prices jumped 10% this week.
- US urged ships to use a southern route hugging Oman's coast; Iran says this violates the June MOU.
